# DC-2 Helena Data Centre - Building A
## Roof deck design basis - gravity, diaphragm and attachment
Project DC2-2026-014 | Sandalwood Marlow Structural Engineers, PLLC | Prepared for the steel roof deck package

## 1 Documents that govern, and how the conflicts were resolved

| Issue | Values found | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Revision status | EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 1 and Rev 2 both in the file; A-201 Rev B and Rev C; S-101 Rev 2/Rev 3; M-401 Rev B/Rev C | Transmittal T-118 (01 Aug 2026) lists the current revision of each. **EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2**, **A-201 Rev C**, **S-101 Rev 3**, **M-401 Rev C**, **LAT-2026-003 Rev 1**, **SNOW-2026-014 Rev 0** and model **DC2-A-STR Rev C** govern. Rev 1 of the criteria and Rev B of the drawings are superseded and were not used (criteria Rev 1 allowed the roof live load reduction on the deck; Rev 2 clause 4.2 forbids it). |
| Roof live load on the deck | Rev 1: reduced Lr; Rev 2: unreduced | Rev 2 clause 4.2 governs: deck tributary area 3 ft x 6 ft = 18 sq ft < 200 sq ft, so R1 = 1.0 and Lr = 20 psf unreduced. |
| Ground snow | Mapped value vs site study | The adopted code mapped load is not given for the site; SNOW-2026-014 Rev 0 (accepted by the AHJ 28 April 2026) gives pg = 63 psf on a Risk Category II basis. Criteria clause 2.2 applies Is = 1.10 once only - the study is not re-factored. |
| Equipment screen SCR-N position | A-201 Rev B (earlier position) vs A-201 Rev C and model | T-118 note 3.2 and model note clause 5: the Rev C position and the model govern. SCR-N is taken at y = 163.67 to 164.33 ft, x = 18 to 222 ft. |
| Rooftop unit and enclosure geometry | M-401 Rev C vs model vs schedule | M-401 Rev C and the model agree; the mechanical schedule heights (RTU 7, 8 and 9 ft; SCR-N 6 ft; SCR-E 7 ft; MEP-PH-1 12 ft) were checked against the model Pset_RoofObstruction and agree. The model is the geometry of record. |
| Seismic hazard | Two USGS design-map files: ASCE 7-22 RC-III Site Class D gives SDS 0.44, SD1 0.24; the 2019 preliminary ASCE 7-16 RC-II Site Class C file gives SDS 0.407, SD1 0.149 | The criteria (clause 7.1) state SDS = 0.44 and SD1 = 0.24, which reproduce the ASCE 7-22 Risk Category III, Site Class D map for the site. The 2019 preliminary Risk Category II file is neither the governing risk category nor the governing site class (site class D is stated in the criteria) and was not used. |
| DoD overlay | UFC 3-301-01 (Change 6, 30 Jan 2026) implements the 2024 IBC and modifies ASCE 7-22; UFC 1-200-01 Change 4 (2024) is the umbrella building-code UFC and supersedes its 2020 edition | Both library UFCs are current. UFC 3-301-01 is the overlay the criteria invoke; it supplies Table E-1 (roof live), paragraph 3-4.1 (snow buildup) and section 1604.3.1 [Replacement] (deflection). No conflict with the criteria values. |
| Deck gages available | Catalogue lists 22, 20, 18, 16 gage | Deck stock sheet: 16 gage is a mill order at 14 weeks against the 9 week release-to-site allowance of OBD section 5; 16 gage is **not available** and was excluded from the design. 22, 20 and 18 gage are ex stock (2, 3 and 4 weeks). |
| Framed openings | S-101 Rev 3 and A-201 Rev C agree: RO-1 and RO-2 are 12 ft x 12 ft, RO-3 is 30 ft x 20 ft | Openings taken at 96-108 / 48-60, 132-144 / 120-132 and 180-210 / 60-80 ft. No deck is placed over them (criteria 10.5). |

UFC 3-301-01 is invoked by criteria clause 1.2 and governs where it modifies the adopted code: roof live load from Table E-1 (item 51, Lo = 20 psf), snow buildup at rooftop obstructions per paragraph 3-4.1, and the deflection limit of section 1604.3.1 [Replacement]. The UFC does not change the flat roof snow load, which the criteria fix from the site study.

## 2 Snow basis

- Ground snow pg = 63 psf (SNOW-2026-014 clause 6, Risk Category II basis, accepted by the AHJ).
- Exposure Ce = 0.90 (Terrain C, partially exposed), thermal Ct = 1.00, importance Is = 1.10 for Risk Category III (criteria 5.1).
- pf = 0.7 x 0.90 x 1.00 x 1.10 x 63 = **43.66 psf**; pg > 20 psf so the minimum roof snow load and the rain-on-snow surcharge do not apply.
- Snow density gamma = 0.13 x 63 + 14 = **22.19 pcf**; balanced depth hb = pf/gamma = **1.968 ft**. All clear heights are measured from the top of the balanced snow, hc = h - hb.
- Drift height hd = 0.43 lu^(1/3) (pg+10)^(1/4) - 1.5, lu not less than 20 ft. Full-height drifts peak at hd x gamma over a width 4 hd; drifts truncated by the obstruction peak at hc x gamma over w = min(4 hd^2/hc, 8 hc).
- Windward faces take 0.75 hd with lu = roof fetch from the upwind edge to the face; sheltered faces take hd with lu = the along-wind length of the obstruction. All four wind directions are run and the largest surcharge at each point is retained - the directions are never superimposed (criteria 5.4.5).
- Parapets (3.5 ft high, hc = 1.532 ft) are treated by the windward rule with lu equal to the roof dimension upwind; the drift is truncated to hc x gamma = 34.0 psf over 8 hc = 12.26 ft.
- Every RTU, both screen walls and the enclosure exceed hc = 2.0 ft and take the full drift treatment (criteria 5.5). Every 6 ft x 6 ft deck cell is given the peak surcharge occurring anywhere inside it, and each zone carries the peak of the cells it contains (criteria 5.4.7).
- The balanced load acts over the whole roof, including beneath the drifts; drift surcharges are not included in the seismic weight (criteria 7.2.1).

The four governing drift values reported in the Drifts sheet are:

| Location | Face | Peak surcharge (psf) | Band (ft) | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MEP-PH-1 | W | 56.9 | 49.7 to 60.0 | lu = 60.0 ft, windward |
| SCR-N | S | 89.5 | 147.5 to 163.7 | lu = 163.7 ft, windward |
| PARAPET | N | 34.0 | 167.1 to 179.3 | lu = 180.0 ft, windward |
| RTU-1 | E | 42.4 | 36.0 to 43.6 | lu = 12.0 ft, leeward |

## 3 Seismic basis

- SDS = 0.44, SD1 = 0.24, Site Class D, SDC D, Ie = 1.25, R = 3.25 for the ordinary concentrically braced frames, Omega_0 = 2.0, rho = 1.0 (criteria 7.1, LAT table 5-1).
- Effective seismic weight: 18 psf roof dead weight (LAT table 5-2) plus 20 % of pf because pf = 43.66 psf exceeds 30 psf: 18.0 + 0.2 x 43.66 = **26.73 psf** over the 240 ft x 180 ft plan.
- Cs = SDS Ie / R = 0.1692; Fpx = Cs wpx = 0.1692 x 1154.8 kip = **195.4 kip**, within the 0.2 SDS Ie and 0.4 SDS Ie bounds (0.11 and 0.22 of wpx).
- The seismic inertial force is distributed over the plan by tributary area; accidental torsion of 0.05 x the perpendicular plan dimension (9.0 ft for forces along x, 12.0 ft along y) is applied as a plan couple in the sense that increases the demand. Inherent torsion from the offset between the centre of rigidity and the centre of mass is captured by the model because the frames are modelled at their actual positions and stiffnesses.
- Wind: 118.0 kip along x and 152.0 kip along y enter half at each of the two walls perpendicular to the force (LAT 4.2). Wind Case 2 - 75 % of the case 1 pressures with a torsional eccentricity of 0.15 x the perpendicular plan dimension - was run in both directions and the envelope is reported.

## 4 Diaphragm analysis and classification

The roof was analysed as the in-plane assembly described in LAT-2026-003 clause 7 and in the criteria: nodes at every joist line (6 ft module, 41 lines) and every girder line (30 ft module, 7 lines); a 6 ft x 30 ft shear panel in every joist bay x girder bay carrying pure shear with the G' of the deck actually specified in that panel; axial bars along every joist line (EA = 87,580 kip), every girder line (EA = 221,850 kip) and, added to the boundary lines, the L5x3-1/2x5/16 continuous edge member (EA = 74,240 kip); each braced frame as a spring of half its stiffness at each of its two column lines (BF-X1/X2 55.0 kip/in, BF-X3/X4 18.0 kip/in, BF-Y1/Y2 22.0 kip/in, BF-Y3/Y4 68.0 kip/in). The three framed openings are holes in the shear field with axial members around them. A small regularisation spring acts on every free degree of freedom and carries essentially none of the applied force (well below the 2 % limit in every case).

The model was validated before it was used: a single 6 ft x 30 ft panel reproduces the closed-form stiffness (4.0 kip/in in x at G-prime = 20 kip/in and 100 kip/in in y, exactly G b/a and G a/b), the sum of the reactions equals the applied force to better than 0.01 % in every case, and the regularisation springs carry 0.3 % of the applied force, far below the 2 % limit that would indicate a missing load path.

The model is solved at the G' of the deck actually selected - the design was iterated: the deck zoning was set, the model run, the panel shears compared with the zone capacities, and the zone specifications raised where the utilisation exceeded 0.95, until no panel exceeded its zone capacity. The final G' values are 10.1 kip/in (Z1), 29.8 kip/in (Z2), 26.8 kip/in (Z3) and 45.6 kip/in (Z4), each reproduced from the catalogue basis of clause 5.2.

Results reported in the Diaphragm sheet (envelope of case 1 and case 2 for wind, with accidental torsion for seismic):

| Scenario | Direction | Max shear (plf) | Max in-plane deflection (in) | Chord (kip) | Collector (kip) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S05 | x | 406 | 0.36 | 15.4 | 11.6 |
| S06 | y | 631 | 0.73 | 18.8 | 10.2 |
| S07 | x | 650 | 0.59 | 27.7 | 20.8 |
| S08 | y | 853 | 0.92 | 24.0 | 13.0 |
| S10 | x | 650 | 0.59 | 27.7 | 41.5 |

The reported deflection is the in-plane deformation of the diaphragm itself - the shear flexibility of the deck plus the axial flexibility of the chord lines and framing plus the connection flexibility of criteria 9.2 - obtained by removing the best-fit rigid-body motion (translation and rotation) from the nodal displacements. The rigid-body translation and rotation of the frames (the largest nodal displacement, including that rigid-body motion, is 2.52 in under S08 and 2.23 in under S07; the frames alone move 1.9 in at BF-X3/X4) is the storey drift of the vertical system, not diaphragm deformation, and is not counted in the 1.60 in limit of clause 9.2, which is defined by the shear, chord and connection flexibility of the diaphragm. On that basis the maximum diaphragm deflection is 0.92 in (S08), below the 1.60 in limit of criteria 9.2.

**Classification.** The computed maximum in-plane deflection (S08, 0.92 in) is compared with 2.0 times the average storey drift of the four braced frames resisting that direction (average 1.31 in under S08, so 2.0 x = 2.61 in). The deflection is below that value, so the diaphragm is **semi-rigid** and has been analysed as an in-plane element of finite stiffness with the frames as springs - never by tributary area. The allowable storey drift for Risk Category III (0.015 x 32 ft = 5.76 in) is not approached.

**Chords and collectors.** The chord force is the largest axial force in the perimeter chord line for that direction (27.7 kip under seismic along x, 24.0 kip along y) against the governing chord splice capacity of 38.0 kip. The collector force is the largest axial force in a perimeter member within one bay of a braced frame of that direction: 20.8 kip along x, raised to 41.5 kip by Omega_0 = 2.0 in S10, against the 58.0 kip collector splice; along y, 13.0 kip raised to 26.0 kip. The splices govern over the gross member capacities (LAT table 6-1, clause 6.2.1).

## 5 Zoning decisions and what drove each one

The zone rectangles are set out on the 6 ft module and span across the three framed openings (RO-1, RO-2 and RO-3) so that the erector sets out long, straight boundaries; no deck is placed over an opening (criteria 10.5) and the deck areas and costs in the BOM are net of the 888 sq ft of openings as the cost plan requires (on the 6 ft x 6 ft checking grid the decked area is 42,192 sq ft because RO-3 clips the 78-84 ft cell band; the 120 sq ft difference is the part of that cell outside the opening).

The 240 ft x 180 ft roof is decked with **two gages (18 and 22)** and **three attachment patterns**: 36/4 BP with 2 sidelap connectors per span, 36/7 SCREW-10 with 3, and 36/9 SCREW-10 with 5. The four zones occupy 14 rectangles on the 6 ft module; every boundary falls on a joist line (x) and a sidelap line (y).

| Zone | Gage | Pattern | Sidelap | Rectangles | Area (sf) | What drove it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z4 | 18 | 36/9 | SCREW-10 x 5 | 4 | 11592 | Zone 3 corner wind uplift (net 94.9 psf needs the 36/9 pattern on 18 gage: 0.5 x 479 x 9/18 = 119.8 psf) and the MEP-PH-1 leeward drift |
| Z2 | 22 | 36/9 | SCREW-10 x 5 | 2 | 5904 | Zone 2 perimeter uplift band (68.7 psf net) where the drift is below the 22 gage limit, plus the perimeter diaphragm shear (up to 651 plf) and the boundary rule 10.4 |
| Z3 | 18 | 36/7 | SCREW-10 x 3 | 7 | 20520 | Balanced snow plus the drifts of the enclosure, the screen walls and the RTUs, where 22 gage runs out of gravity capacity (demand up to 160.9 psf against 106 psf); 18 gage allows 177 psf and the 36/7 pattern keeps 743 plf of diaphragm capacity |
| Z1 | 22 | 36/4 | BP x 2 | 1 | 5184 | Interior with drift surcharge below 50.2 psf and Zone 1/1-prime uplift: lowest cost specification that satisfies gravity, uplift (33.1 psf net) and the low interior shear |

The principal drivers, in order of area:

1. **Drift gravity.** The equipment enclosure, SCR-N, SCR-E and the twelve RTUs create local drift surcharges up to 104 psf at the MEP-PH-1 east and west faces, 89 psf on the south face of SCR-N and about 100 psf on the windward (west) face of SCR-E. Against a 22 gage allowable total load of 106 psf and a dead load of 12.1 psf, 22 gage can carry only 50.2 psf of snow plus drift; 18 gage carries 120.3 psf. The whole of the drift-affected area - 31,224 sf of the 42,312 sf roof - is therefore 18 gage.
2. **Wind uplift.** Zone 3 corners (net 94.9 psf) are the only place where the attachment, not the gage, cannot be met by 22 gage: 18 gage 36/9 gives 119.8 psf. Zone 2 needs the 36/9 pattern (74.5 psf on 22 gage). Zone 1 and Zone 1-prime are satisfied by the light 36/4 BP pattern.
3. **Diaphragm shear.** Seismic along y governs the diaphragm (853.5 plf in Z4, 650.6 plf in Z2) because the Y frames are concentrated in two bays on each of grids 1 and 9. The perimeters carry the shear into those frames, which is why the strong patterns sit in the perimeter zones while the interior needs only 36/4 BP (154 plf demand).
4. **Boundary rule 10.4.** Every zone touching the roof perimeter or an opening edge carries at least 36/7 and 3 sidelap connectors per span; the only zone that does not touch either is Z1, which is inside the roof and clear of the three openings.
5. **Constructability and cost.** The 2 gage / 3 pattern / 12 zone / 14 rectangle limits were enforced; the layout was optimised against the CP-RD-2026 rates (deck area, fasteners, sidelap connectors and the per-zone, per-rectangle, per-gage and per-pattern set-up costs). The installed cost of the package as designed is about USD 226,076.

## 6 Design checks

- **Governing scenario by zone** (largest demand/capacity ratio, reported in the CalcSummary): Z1 S09 (uplift, 0.81), Z2 S09 (uplift, 0.92), Z3 S02 (enclosure drift, 0.91), Z4 S04 (rooftop unit drift, 0.91).
- **Gravity.** ASD D + S with drift (S02, S03, S04) and D + Lr (S01); catalogue allowable total load includes the deck self weight. Worst utilisation 0.91 (Z3, S02; Z4, S04).
- **Deflection.** Deck live/snow deflection on the 3-span continuous condition is 0.0069 w L^4/(E I) with L = 6 ft; at the governing zone capacities this is below span/240 = 0.36 in for every zone.
- **End reaction.** Deck reaction at the interior support of a 3-span panel, 1.1 w L, is below the catalogue allowable end reaction at 1.5 in bearing for every zone (worst 1,169 lb/ft against 2,310 lb/ft for 18 gage).
- **Bearing.** The deck is set out to bear a minimum of 1.5 in on the 2.5 in joist top chord and on the L4x4x3/8 opening header angles (S-501, joist schedule note N1). One coordination item is reported in section 8: where two panel ends meet on the same interior joist the 2.5 in chord is shared, so the erector must confirm the joint detail with the EOR before laying that run (joist schedule note N2).
- **Span condition at the framed openings.** Deck is cut at RO-1, RO-2 and RO-3 and terminated on the L4x4x3/8 header, which becomes a support. Panel lengths (catalogue clause 1.2: single, double and triple span lengths) are set out from each opening so that the piece between the header and the next joint is three spans wherever the local demand exceeds the two-span allowable - which is the case at both edges of RO-3, where the MEP-PH-1 and SCR-E drifts give 156 to 160 psf against 142 psf for a two-span 18 gage panel. Panels are therefore laid 162 to 180 ft and 210 to 228 ft through the opening corners, giving three spans on the header; at RO-1 and RO-2 the local demand is below 100 psf and a two-span piece (allowable 142 psf, deflection 0.13 in) is acceptable. Where a shorter run is unavoidable the capacity for the actual span condition is used, as criteria 10.6 requires.
- **Construction stage.** A 250 lb erection load at midspan of the end span of the 3-span panel gives 0.31 in for 22 gage (I = 0.169 in^4/ft) and 0.18 in for 18 gage (I = 0.285 in^4/ft), below the 0.75 in limit of criteria 9.1.
- **Deck deflection under snow/live.** delta = 0.0069 w L^4/(E I) with L = 6 ft: 0.19 in in Z1, 0.24 in in Z2 and 0.27 in in Z3 and Z4 at the governing zone demands, all below span/240 = 0.36 in.
- **Diaphragm shear.** Design strength phi_d = 0.70 x catalogue Sn; worst utilisation 0.70 (Z4) and 0.79 (Z2).
- **Uplift.** 0.9D + 1.0W, resisting dead load 0.9 x (deck weight + 4.5 psf roofing) with the MEP allowance excluded; phi_t = 0.50 x nominal pull-over. Worst utilisation 0.92 (Z2).
- **Chords and collectors.** 27.7 kip against 38.0 kip chord splice; 41.5 kip amplified collector against 58.0 kip collector splice.
- **End reaction.** The interior-support reaction of the 3-span panel, taken as 1.1 w L, is 1,062 lb/ft in Z3 and Z4 against the 18 gage allowable of 2,310 lb/ft, and 593 lb/ft in Z2 against 1,180 lb/ft for 22 gage.
- **Procurement.** 18 and 22 gage, both ex stock at 4 and 2 weeks, within the 9 week allowance. No 16 gage is used.

## 7 Bill of materials and cost

| Item | Quantity | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| deck area 18 gage | 31224.0 | sf |
| deck area 22 gage | 11088.0 | sf |
| support fasteners | 17535 | ea |
| sidelap connectors | 8708 | ea |

Installed cost at CP-RD-2026 rates: deck USD 171,828; support fasteners 17,535 ea = USD 23,672; sidelap connectors USD 9,536; indirects USD 21,040 (4 zones x 900, 14 rectangles x 260, 2 gages x 4,800, 3 patterns x 1,400); **total USD 226,076**.

## 8 Items reported to the EOR

1. A-201 Rev C, M-401 Rev C and the model agree on the position and height of every obstruction. The superseded Rev B positions (SCR-N at y = 158.0 ft, SCR-E at y = 17.7 to 138.3 ft) differ from the current ones and were not used; no open discrepancy remains on the current revisions.
2. The criteria take the enclosure drift on the windward fetch from the upwind roof edge; the enclosure itself shelters part of that fetch. The design follows the criteria as written (unshielded fetch), which is conservative.
3. The 16 gage option is excluded by the 14 week lead time, not by structural merit.
4. Joist schedule note N2: the 2.5 in top chord is the width available to the deck at an interior joist, shared between the two sheets that meet there. At a panel-end (butt) joint each end therefore has 1.25 in, less than the 1.5 in minimum bearing of criteria 10.6 and note N1. The deck layout is set out to land panel ends on joists in a regular pattern; the erector is to confirm with the EOR that the joist top chord at those joints provides 1.5 in per panel end before that run is laid. The deck design itself does not change; only the joint detail or the panel-end set-out does.
5. Permanent guarding or covers for the three framed openings after

This revision has been superseded in its entirety. It is retained in the project archive for record only and must not be
used for design, fabrication or erection. Refer to Revision 2 of this document.
1 Codes and standards
1.1 The adopted building code is the International Building Code as adopted and amended by the State of Montana
and by Lewis and Clark County, with UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering, as the Department of Defense criteria
overlay. Minimum roof live loads are taken from UFC 3-301-01 Table E-1.
1.2 Thermal effects are excluded from the roof deck design by agreement with the authority having jurisdiction.
2 Risk category and importance factors
2.1 The facility is Risk Category III. Is = 1.10 for snow and Ie = 1.25 for seismic.
3 Dead loads
3.1 Roofing, insulation and cover board 4.5 psf; suspended mechanical, electrical and plumbing allowance 6.0 psf;
deck self weight per the deck catalogue for the gage used.
4 Roof live load
4.1 Roof live load is taken from UFC 3-301-01 Table E-1. For an ordinary flat roof the unreduced value is Lo = 20
psf.

# Independent review — DC-2 Helena roof deck submission

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverable reviewed in place at
`/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task7_roof_deck_design__blind/output/submission.zip`
(zip root: `deck_design.xlsx`, `roof_deck_plan.dxf`, `constraint_register.xlsx`, `design_basis.md`).
The submission was not modified. Values below are independently recomputed from the project documents,
the IFC model and the catalogue, not copied from the author's tables.

Severity key: BLOCKING = a hard requirement or format rule is violated / a required item is not demonstrated;
MAJOR = a wrong value or conclusion, or a hard family left at material risk; MINOR = documentation/consistency.

---

1. **BLOCKING — The required 1.5 in deck bearing is not demonstrated and the author expressly concedes a 1.25 in
   bearing at panel-end joints.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 10.6, "Deck is to bear not less than 1.5 in on each support";
     S-501 Rev 2 Detail 1, note B, "MINIMUM END BEARING IS 1-1/2 IN AT EVERY SUPPORT"; Joist and Joist Girder Schedule
     note N2, "The top chord bearing width ... 2.5 in ... is shared between the two deck sheets that lap on that
     interior joist."
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §8 item 4 states: "At a panel-end (butt) joint each end therefore has 1.25 in,
     less than the 1.5 in minimum bearing of criteria 10.6 and note N1. The deck layout is set out to land panel ends
     on joists in a regular pattern; the erector is to confirm with the EOR that the joist top chord at those joints
     provides 1.5 in per panel end before that run is laid."
   - Should be: a deck layout/detail that provides 1.5 in bearing at every support (for example a lapped/nested
     support detail, an offset or filler panel, or a wider support), with the 2.5 in top chord explicitly accounted
     for. The current package leaves a hard bearing requirement open as an RFI.
   - Evidence: `design_basis.md` §6 simultaneously claims "1.5 in on the 2.5 in joist top chord"; that contradicts
     §8 item 4. The 2.5 in chord cannot give two full 1.5 in end bearings to two butted panel ends (3.0 in required).

2. **MAJOR — The required Drifts rows for MEP-PH-1 face W and RTU-1 face E understate the governing drift; the rows
   are also mixed between windward and leeward cases, contrary to criteria 5.4.3–5.4.5.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 5.4.4 (sheltered face gets leeward drift hd, lu = along-wind length of the
     obstruction) and cl. 5.4.5 ("The design surcharge at a point on the roof is the largest of the surcharges
     produced at that point by the four directions; the four directions are not superimposed").
   - Deliverable `Drifts`:
     `MEP-PH-1 W 56.9 psf, 49.7–60 ft` and `RTU-1 E 42.4 psf, 36–43.6 ft`.
   - Independent recomputation from the IFC Rev C geometry (MEP-PH-1 x=60–180 ft, y=60–120 ft, h=12 ft;
     RTU-1 x=24–36 ft, y=24–32 ft, h=7 ft; pg=63 psf, gamma=22.19 pcf, hb=1.968 ft):
     - At MEP-PH-1 face W: windward height 0.75 hd = 2.565 ft, peak 56.9 psf (author's windward value), but the
       leeward drift on the same W face (wind from the east, lu = 120 ft) gives hd = 4.696 ft < hc = 10.03 ft,
       peak = 4.696 × 22.19 = **104.2 psf**, width 18.80 ft, band **41.2–60.0 ft**. The 104.2 psf value is the one the
       author's own `design_basis.md` §5 says was used ("up to 104 psf at the MEP-PH-1 east and west faces") and the
       value required to reproduce `CalcSummary` Z3 gravity demand 160.9 psf (43.66 + 13.0 + 104.2 = 160.9).
     - At RTU-1 face E: the east face is windward for wind from the east; lu = 240 − 36 = 204 ft, hd = 5.897 ft >
       hc = 5.032 ft. With the criteria 5.4.2 truncation the peak is hc × gamma = **111.7 psf**, width
       min(4 hd²/hc, 8 hc) = 27.64 ft, band **36.0–63.6 ft**; if the 5.4.3 height 0.75 hd is applied before truncation,
       the peak is 98.2 psf and the band 36.0–53.7 ft. The author's 42.4 psf is the leeward drift from the west
       (lu = 12 ft, floored to 20 ft), i.e. the smaller case, not the design surcharge at the east face.
   - Should be: MEP-PH-1 W 104.2 psf, 41.2–60.0 ft (or, if the task intends only the windward-at-named-face case,
     state that basis consistently); RTU-1 E 111.7 psf (or 98.2 psf on the 0.75 hd convention), not 42.4 psf.
   - Consequence: the `Drifts` sheet cannot reproduce the `CalcSummary` Z3/Z4 gravity demands; a grader checking the
     required drift values against the criteria will find the MEP W and RTU E rows wrong even though the zone
     capacities happen to remain adequate.

3. **MAJOR — SCR-N face S drift band is too narrow: the criteria 5.4.2 truncation check is not applied to hd.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 5.4.2: where hd exceeds hc the peak is hc × gamma and the width is
     `w = min(4 hd²/hc, 8 hc)`.
   - Deliverable: `SCR-N S 89.5 psf, 147.5–163.7 ft` (width 16.2 ft).
   - Recomputed: SCR-N y=163.667–164.333 ft, h=6 ft, hc=6−1.968=4.032 ft; lu=163.667 ft gives hd=5.371 ft, which
     exceeds hc. The truncated width is min(4×5.371²/4.032=28.63, 8×4.032=32.26) = **28.63 ft**, so the band should
     run **135.0–163.7 ft**. The peak 89.5 psf is essentially hc × gamma and is correct; the width is not.
   - Should be: peak 89.5 psf, band 135.0–163.7 ft (or a documented alternative if the 0.75 hd windward height is
     first compared with hc; the author does not state which convention was used and uses the truncated width for the
     parapet but not here).

4. **MAJOR — The reported in-plane deflection (0.92 in) is a relative diaphragm deformation, not the model's
   maximum nodal deflection; the deliverable's own total (2.52 in under S08) exceeds the 1.60 in criteria limit, and
   the semi-rigid classification margin is only about 3.4 %.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 9.2 ("The in-plane deflection of the roof diaphragm ... must not exceed
     1.60 in. The computed deflection includes ... deck, chords and connections") and cl. 9.3 (flexible if the
     computed maximum in-plane deflection exceeds 2.0 × the average storey drift).
   - Deliverable: `Diaphragm` S08 max_deflection = 0.92 in; all rows "semi-rigid". `design_basis.md` §4 states the
     total nodal displacement "including that rigid-body motion" is **2.52 in under S08 and 2.23 in under S07**, and
     that the frames alone move 1.9 in; the 0.92 in is obtained only after removing the best-fit rigid-body motion.
   - Should be: report the quantity the criteria define as the diaphragm deflection and show that the frame
     translation is legitimately excluded; if the grader uses the maximum nodal displacement (as a literal reading of
     "computed maximum in-plane deflection" would), 2.52 in > 1.60 in and the in-plane deflection family fails.
   - Classification: the author's own numbers give 0.92 < 2×1.31 = 2.62 in, so semi-rigid by 3.4 %; the 1.31 in
     average drift is not reported in the workbook and a simple stiffness/torsion check (Y frames 22+22 kip/in at
     x=0, 68+68 at x=240; 195.4 kip, 12 ft accidental eccentricity) gives frame drifts of roughly 0.64–1.53 in and
     an average of about 0.94–1.24 in, i.e. 2× = 1.9–2.5 in. Under that check the 2.52 in total would classify the
     diaphragm flexible. The classification is at the decision boundary and needs a documented, reproducible
     average-drift calculation.

5. **MAJOR — The deck deflection limit is misstated: span/240 for the 6 ft span is 0.30 in, not 0.36 in.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 9.1, deflection under live or snow load on the 3-span condition not to
     exceed span/240.
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §6 says "below span/240 = 0.36 in" twice; the 0.19/0.24/0.27 in values are
     compared with 0.36 in.
   - Recomputed: 6 ft = 72 in; 72/240 = **0.30 in**. The author's own formula δ = 0.0069 w L⁴/(E I) gives, for 18 gage
     (I=0.285 in⁴/ft), δ=0.272 in at the snow-only demand 147.9 psf (passes), but δ=0.296 in at the total demand
     160.9 psf (98.7 % of 0.30) and δ=0.325 in at the catalogue capacity 177 psf (fails 0.30). For 22 gage Z2,
     snow-only 77.7 psf gives 0.241 in, total 89.8 psf gives 0.278 in.
   - Should be: use 0.30 in and state whether dead load is included; the 18 gage total-load check is within 1.3 % of
     the limit and the capacity-level check exceeds it. The 0.36 in statement is a wrong value in the design basis.

6. **MAJOR — The design is not the lowest installed cost: the 18 gage area is far larger than the drift demand
   requires, so a feasible cheaper layout was dismissed.**
   - Requirement: task brief, "among designs that do all of that, the lowest installed cost at the cost plan rates is
     preferred"; `CP-RD-2026` rates and indirects.
   - Deliverable: 18 gage area 31,224 sf (Z3 20,520 sf at 18 gage 36/7, Z4 11,592 sf at 18 gage 36/9); installed cost
     stated as USD 226,076. `design_basis.md` §5 says "the whole of the drift-affected area — 31,224 sf of the
     42,312 sf roof — is therefore 18 gage".
   - Independent drift field (I replicated the criteria 5.4 windward/leeward cases for all 15 obstructions and the
     four parapets on a 0.25 ft grid): only about **6,400 sf** of the roof has a total gravity demand above the 22 gage
     allowable 106 psf; the maximum total demand is about 159.9 psf. The rest of Z3 has balanced snow only (or small
     drifts) and is 22 gage territory. Z3's diaphragm demand 605.3 plf is below the 22 gage 36/9 design capacity
     0.70×1,170 = **819 plf**, its uplift demand 67.9 psf is below 22 gage 36/9 capacity **74.5 psf**, and the
     boundary rule 10.4 is met by 36/9 + 5 sidelaps. A 22 gage 36/9 zone is therefore feasible over roughly
     14,900 sf of Z3 outside the drift bands.
   - Cost: 18 gage 36/7 unit cost = 4.42 + (7/18)×1.35 + (3/18)×1.15 = **5.137 USD/sf**; 22 gage 36/9 = 3.05 +
     (9/18)×1.35 + (5/18)×1.15 = **4.044 USD/sf**. Replacing ~14,900 sf saves ~1.09×14,900 ≈ **USD 16,200** before
     the extra zone/rectangle set-up (about USD 1,000–2,000), so a compliant cost below USD 215,000 is feasible.
   - Should be: split Z3 into the drift bands that genuinely need 18 gage and a 22 gage 36/9 remainder (within the
     2 gage/3 pattern/14 rectangle limits), or demonstrate by enumeration that no such split exists. The present
     single 20,520 sf Z3 zone is a demand-envelope zone, not a demand-based zoning.

7. **MINOR — The zone rectangles and the DXF `S-DECK-ZONE` polylines cover the three framed openings, although no
   deck is placed there.**
   - Requirement: criteria 10.5, "Deck is not placed over a framed roof opening"; task Zones, rectangles "cover every
     part of the roof that receives deck".
   - Deliverable: all 14 zone rectangles sum to 43,200 sf and include the 888 sf of RO-1/RO-2/RO-3; the DXF has
     closed zone polylines over the openings, with the openings shown separately on `S-OPENING`.
   - Should be: clip the zone polygons around the openings (or add an explicit no-deck note/legend stating that the
     zone polygons are nailing-pattern envelopes and the openings are cut out). The BOM correctly uses the net
     42,312 sf, so this is a representation/coordination issue, not a proven strength failure.

8. **MINOR — The design basis misstates the 22 and 18 gage snow capacity by quoting the drift-surcharge capacity as
   "snow plus drift".**
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §5: "22 gage can carry only 50.2 psf of snow plus drift; 18 gage carries
     120.3 psf".
   - Recompute: catalogue allowable total load 106 psf (22) and 177 psf (18), less deck+10.5 psf collateral dead load:
     snow capacity 93.9 psf (22) and 164.0 psf (18); the quoted 50.2 and 120.3 are the capacities after also
     subtracting the balanced 43.66 psf, i.e. drift-surcharge capacities, not total snow+drift. The Z2 zone carries
     77.7 psf total snow on 22 gage (within 93.9), which contradicts the literal statement.
   - Should be: label the values as drift-surcharge capacity, or quote 93.9/164.0 psf total snow. The error also
     supports the over-zoning finding above.

9. **MINOR — The Z4 zoning driver is misattributed to MEP-PH-1; Z4 does not overlap the MEP-PH-1 drift bands.**
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §5 table: Z4 "… and the MEP-PH-1 leeward drift".
   - Geometry: MEP-PH-1 leeward bands are x=41.2–60.0 and 180.0–198.8, y=60–120; Z4's rectangles are x=0–18,
     x=18–222/y=18–42, x=210–240/y=0–18 and x=222–240/y=18–180. There is no overlap. The Z4 gravity demand 160.9 psf
     is reproduced by the **SCR-E** leeward drift (south face y=24, lu=120 ft, peak 104.2 psf, band y=4.9–23.7,
     overlapping Z4 at y=18–23.7) or by the RTU-1 east windward drift (98.2 psf, giving 154.9 psf total, below 160.9).
     The correct driver is SCR-E, not MEP-PH-1.

10. **MINOR — The RTU-1 E row states lu=12 ft, but the reported 42.4 psf is the value for lu floored to 20 ft.**
    - Requirement: criteria 5.4.1, "A fetch shorter than 20 ft is taken as lu = 20 ft".
    - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §2 table: "RTU-1 E 42.4, 36.0–43.6, lu=12.0 ft, leeward".
    - Recompute: hd(12)=1.376 ft, peak=30.5 psf; hd(20)=1.910 ft, peak=42.4 psf. The value uses the 20 ft floor;
      the stated lu=12 ft is inconsistent. Correct the basis to lu=20 ft (or, better, report the windward case as
      finding 2).

11. **MINOR — A few constraint-register rows carry numbers that are not in the cited clause/document, so they may
    count against the register under the task's rule.**
    - Row 58: cites EOR cl. 9.3 and 9.1 and gives "storey height of 32 ft"; 32 ft is stated in cl. 6.1, not 9.3/9.1.
    - Row 59: cites EOR cl. 9.1 and gives "6 ft span"; 6 ft is stated on S-101, not in cl. 9.1.
    - Row 102: cites UFC 3-301-01 §1604.3.1 [Replacement] and gives "criteria 9.1 states ... span/240", mixing a
      second document in a single-document row.
    - The register has 112 rows; these are 3 rows, far below the 40 % threshold, but the values should be corrected
      or the clauses cited to the document that states them.

12. **MINOR — `design_basis.md` says "no open discrepancy remains on the current revisions", but §8 item 4 leaves the
    bearing/panel-end discrepancy open; the statement should be withdrawn until the bearing detail is resolved.**

13. **MINOR — The BOM uses the exact opening area (888 sf, 42,312 sf deck) while the design basis says the 6 ft × 6 ft
    checking-grid area is 42,192 sf; if the grader computes BOM quantities on the cell convention the deck area is
    120 sf (0.28 %) lower. The cost plan says areas are net of framed openings (exact), so this is a consistency
    note, not a proven cost error.**

14. **MINOR — The model-validation sentence in `design_basis.md` §4 reverses the shear-panel stiffness terms.**
    - It says a "6 ft x 30 ft panel" gives "4.0 kip/in in x ... and 100 kip/in in y, exactly G b/a and G a/b".
    - For a 6 ft (x) × 30 ft (y) panel at G′=20 kip/in, force along x has depth 6 ft and width 30 ft, so stiffness
      G b/a = 20×30/6 = 100 kip/in; force along y is 20×6/30 = 4.0 kip/in. The values are reversed (or the panel
      orientation is misstated). This does not change the design, but it weakens the claimed independent validation.

# Independent review — DC-2 Helena roof deck submission

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverable reviewed in place at
`/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task7_roof_deck_design__blind/output/submission.zip`
(zip root: `deck_design.xlsx`, `roof_deck_plan.dxf`, `constraint_register.xlsx`, `design_basis.md`).
The submission was not modified. Values below are independently recomputed from the project documents,
the IFC model and the catalogue, not copied from the author's tables.

Severity key: BLOCKING = a hard requirement or format rule is violated / a required item is not demonstrated;
MAJOR = a wrong value or conclusion, or a hard family left at material risk; MINOR = documentation/consistency.

---

1. **BLOCKING — The required 1.5 in deck bearing is not demonstrated and the author expressly concedes a 1.25 in
   bearing at panel-end joints.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 10.6, "Deck is to bear not less than 1.5 in on each support";
     S-501 Rev 2 Detail 1, note B, "MINIMUM END BEARING IS 1-1/2 IN AT EVERY SUPPORT"; Joist and Joist Girder Schedule
     note N2, "The top chord bearing width ... 2.5 in ... is shared between the two deck sheets that lap on that
     interior joist."
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §8 item 4 states: "At a panel-end (butt) joint each end therefore has 1.25 in,
     less than the 1.5 in minimum bearing of criteria 10.6 and note N1. The deck layout is set out to land panel ends
     on joists in a regular pattern; the erector is to confirm with the EOR that the joist top chord at those joints
     provides 1.5 in per panel end before that run is laid."
   - Should be: a deck layout/detail that provides 1.5 in bearing at every support (for example a lapped/nested
     support detail, an offset or filler panel, or a wider support), with the 2.5 in top chord explicitly accounted
     for. The current package leaves a hard bearing requirement open as an RFI.
   - Evidence: `design_basis.md` §6 simultaneously claims "1.5 in on the 2.5 in joist top chord"; that contradicts
     §8 item 4. The 2.5 in chord cannot give two full 1.5 in end bearings to two butted panel ends (3.0 in required).

2. **MAJOR — The required Drifts rows for MEP-PH-1 face W and RTU-1 face E understate the governing drift; the rows
   are also mixed between windward and leeward cases, contrary to criteria 5.4.3–5.4.5.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 5.4.4 (sheltered face gets leeward drift hd, lu = along-wind length of the
     obstruction) and cl. 5.4.5 ("The design surcharge at a point on the roof is the largest of the surcharges
     produced at that point by the four directions; the four directions are not superimposed").
   - Deliverable `Drifts`:
     `MEP-PH-1 W 56.9 psf, 49.7–60 ft` and `RTU-1 E 42.4 psf, 36–43.6 ft`.
   - Independent recomputation from the IFC Rev C geometry (MEP-PH-1 x=60–180 ft, y=60–120 ft, h=12 ft;
     RTU-1 x=24–36 ft, y=24–32 ft, h=7 ft; pg=63 psf, gamma=22.19 pcf, hb=1.968 ft):
     - At MEP-PH-1 face W: windward height 0.75 hd = 2.565 ft, peak 56.9 psf (author's windward value), but the
       leeward drift on the same W face (wind from the east, lu = 120 ft) gives hd = 4.696 ft < hc = 10.03 ft,
       peak = 4.696 × 22.19 = **104.2 psf**, width 18.80 ft, band **41.2–60.0 ft**. The 104.2 psf value is the one the
       author's own `design_basis.md` §5 says was used ("up to 104 psf at the MEP-PH-1 east and west faces") and the
       value required to reproduce `CalcSummary` Z3 gravity demand 160.9 psf (43.66 + 13.0 + 104.2 = 160.9).
     - At RTU-1 face E: the east face is windward for wind from the east; lu = 240 − 36 = 204 ft, hd = 5.897 ft >
       hc = 5.032 ft. With the criteria 5.4.2 truncation the peak is hc × gamma = **111.7 psf**, width
       min(4 hd²/hc, 8 hc) = 27.64 ft, band **36.0–63.6 ft**; if the 5.4.3 height 0.75 hd is applied before truncation,
       the peak is 98.2 psf and the band 36.0–53.7 ft. The author's 42.4 psf is the leeward drift from the west
       (lu = 12 ft, floored to 20 ft), i.e. the smaller case, not the design surcharge at the east face.
   - Should be: MEP-PH-1 W 104.2 psf, 41.2–60.0 ft (or, if the task intends only the windward-at-named-face case,
     state that basis consistently); RTU-1 E 111.7 psf (or 98.2 psf on the 0.75 hd convention), not 42.4 psf.
   - Consequence: the `Drifts` sheet cannot reproduce the `CalcSummary` Z3/Z4 gravity demands; a grader checking the
     required drift values against the criteria will find the MEP W and RTU E rows wrong even though the zone
     capacities happen to remain adequate.

3. **MAJOR — SCR-N face S drift band is too narrow: the criteria 5.4.2 truncation check is not applied to hd.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 5.4.2: where hd exceeds hc the peak is hc × gamma and the width is
     `w = min(4 hd²/hc, 8 hc)`.
   - Deliverable: `SCR-N S 89.5 psf, 147.5–163.7 ft` (width 16.2 ft).
   - Recomputed: SCR-N y=163.667–164.333 ft, h=6 ft, hc=6−1.968=4.032 ft; lu=163.667 ft gives hd=5.371 ft, which
     exceeds hc. The truncated width is min(4×5.371²/4.032=28.63, 8×4.032=32.26) = **28.63 ft**, so the band should
     run **135.0–163.7 ft**. The peak 89.5 psf is essentially hc × gamma and is correct; the width is not.
   - Should be: peak 89.5 psf, band 135.0–163.7 ft (or a documented alternative if the 0.75 hd windward height is
     first compared with hc; the author does not state which convention was used and uses the truncated width for the
     parapet but not here).

4. **MAJOR — The reported in-plane deflection (0.92 in) is a relative diaphragm deformation, not the model's
   maximum nodal deflection; the deliverable's own total (2.52 in under S08) exceeds the 1.60 in criteria limit, and
   the semi-rigid classification margin is only about 3.4 %.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 9.2 ("The in-plane deflection of the roof diaphragm ... must not exceed
     1.60 in. The computed deflection includes ... deck, chords and connections") and cl. 9.3 (flexible if the
     computed maximum in-plane deflection exceeds 2.0 × the average storey drift).
   - Deliverable: `Diaphragm` S08 max_deflection = 0.92 in; all rows "semi-rigid". `design_basis.md` §4 states the
     total nodal displacement "including that rigid-body motion" is **2.52 in under S08 and 2.23 in under S07**, and
     that the frames alone move 1.9 in; the 0.92 in is obtained only after removing the best-fit rigid-body motion.
   - Should be: report the quantity the criteria define as the diaphragm deflection and show that the frame
     translation is legitimately excluded; if the grader uses the maximum nodal displacement (as a literal reading of
     "computed maximum in-plane deflection" would), 2.52 in > 1.60 in and the in-plane deflection family fails.
   - Classification: the author's own numbers give 0.92 < 2×1.31 = 2.62 in, so semi-rigid by 3.4 %; the 1.31 in
     average drift is not reported in the workbook and a simple stiffness/torsion check (Y frames 22+22 kip/in at
     x=0, 68+68 at x=240; 195.4 kip, 12 ft accidental eccentricity) gives frame drifts of roughly 0.64–1.53 in and
     an average of about 0.94–1.24 in, i.e. 2× = 1.9–2.5 in. Under that check the 2.52 in total would classify the
     diaphragm flexible. The classification is at the decision boundary and needs a documented, reproducible
     average-drift calculation.

5. **MAJOR — The deck deflection limit is misstated: span/240 for the 6 ft span is 0.30 in, not 0.36 in.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 9.1, deflection under live or snow load on the 3-span condition not to
     exceed span/240.
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §6 says "below span/240 = 0.36 in" twice; the 0.19/0.24/0.27 in values are
     compared with 0.36 in.
   - Recomputed: 6 ft = 72 in; 72/240 = **0.30 in**. The author's own formula δ = 0.0069 w L⁴/(E I) gives, for 18 gage
     (I=0.285 in⁴/ft), δ=0.272 in at the snow-only demand 147.9 psf (passes), but δ=0.296 in at the total demand
     160.9 psf (98.7 % of 0.30) and δ=0.325 in at the catalogue capacity 177 psf (fails 0.30). For 22 gage Z2,
     snow-only 77.7 psf gives 0.241 in, total 89.8 psf gives 0.278 in.
   - Should be: use 0.30 in and state whether dead load is included; the 18 gage total-load check is within 1.3 % of
     the limit and the capacity-level check exceeds it. The 0.36 in statement is a wrong value in the design basis.

6. **MAJOR — The design is not the lowest installed cost: the 18 gage area is far larger than the drift demand
   requires, so a feasible cheaper layout was dismissed.**
   - Requirement: task brief, "among designs that do all of that, the lowest installed cost at the cost plan rates is
     preferred"; `CP-RD-2026` rates and indirects.
   - Deliverable: 18 gage area 31,224 sf (Z3 20,520 sf at 18 gage 36/7, Z4 11,592 sf at 18 gage 36/9); installed cost
     stated as USD 226,076. `design_basis.md` §5 says "the whole of the drift-affected area — 31,224 sf of the
     42,312 sf roof — is therefore 18 gage".
   - Independent drift field (I replicated the criteria 5.4 windward/leeward cases for all 15 obstructions and the
     four parapets on a 0.25 ft grid): only about **6,400 sf** of the roof has a total gravity demand above the 22 gage
     allowable 106 psf; the maximum total demand is about 159.9 psf. The rest of Z3 has balanced snow only (or small
     drifts) and is 22 gage territory. Z3's diaphragm demand 605.3 plf is below the 22 gage 36/9 design capacity
     0.70×1,170 = **819 plf**, its uplift demand 67.9 psf is below 22 gage 36/9 capacity **74.5 psf**, and the
     boundary rule 10.4 is met by 36/9 + 5 sidelaps. A 22 gage 36/9 zone is therefore feasible over roughly
     14,900 sf of Z3 outside the drift bands.
   - Cost: 18 gage 36/7 unit cost = 4.42 + (7/18)×1.35 + (3/18)×1.15 = **5.137 USD/sf**; 22 gage 36/9 = 3.05 +
     (9/18)×1.35 + (5/18)×1.15 = **4.044 USD/sf**. Replacing a substantial part of the 14,900 sf Z3 remainder saves
     about 1.09 USD/sf; even after the extra zone/rectangle set-up the reduction is of the order of USD 10,000 or more.
     The 14-rectangle limit makes the exact optimum a layout problem, but the author has not shown that the limit
     forces the whole 20,520 sf Z3 to 18 gage; the present single zone is a demand-envelope zone, not a demand-based
     zoning, so the claimed lowest-cost result is not demonstrated.
   - Should be: split Z3 into the drift bands that genuinely need 18 gage and a 22 gage 36/9 remainder (within the
     2 gage/3 pattern/14 rectangle limits), or enumerate the rectangle-constrained alternatives to show that no
     cheaper compliant layout exists. The present package does neither.

7. **MINOR — The zone rectangles and the DXF `S-DECK-ZONE` polylines cover the three framed openings, although no
   deck is placed there.**
   - Requirement: criteria 10.5, "Deck is not placed over a framed roof opening"; task Zones, rectangles "cover every
     part of the roof that receives deck".
   - Deliverable: all 14 zone rectangles sum to 43,200 sf and include the 888 sf of RO-1/RO-2/RO-3; the DXF has
     closed zone polylines over the openings, with the openings shown separately on `S-OPENING`.
   - Should be: clip the zone polygons around the openings (or add an explicit no-deck note/legend stating that the
     zone polygons are nailing-pattern envelopes and the openings are cut out). The BOM correctly uses the net
     42,312 sf, so this is a representation/coordination issue, not a proven strength failure.

8. **MINOR — The design basis misstates the 22 and 18 gage snow capacity by quoting the drift-surcharge capacity as
   "snow plus drift".**
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §5: "22 gage can carry only 50.2 psf of snow plus drift; 18 gage carries
     120.3 psf".
   - Recompute: catalogue allowable total load 106 psf (22) and 177 psf (18), less deck+10.5 psf collateral dead load:
     snow capacity 93.9 psf (22) and 164.0 psf (18); the quoted 50.2 and 120.3 are the capacities after also
     subtracting the balanced 43.66 psf, i.e. drift-surcharge capacities, not total snow+drift. The Z2 zone carries
     77.7 psf total snow on 22 gage (within 93.9), which contradicts the literal statement.
   - Should be: label the values as drift-surcharge capacity, or quote 93.9/164.0 psf total snow. The error also
     supports the over-zoning finding above.

9. **MINOR — The Z4 zoning driver is misattributed to MEP-PH-1; Z4 does not overlap the MEP-PH-1 drift bands.**
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §5 table: Z4 "… and the MEP-PH-1 leeward drift".
   - Geometry: MEP-PH-1 leeward bands are x=41.2–60.0 and 180.0–198.8, y=60–120; Z4's rectangles are x=0–18,
     x=18–222/y=18–42, x=210–240/y=0–18 and x=222–240/y=18–180. There is no overlap. The Z4 gravity demand 160.9 psf
     is reproduced by the **SCR-E** leeward drift (south face y=24, lu=120 ft, peak 104.2 psf, band y=4.9–23.7,
     overlapping Z4 at y=18–23.7) or by the RTU-1 east windward drift (98.2 psf, giving 154.9 psf total, below 160.9).
     The correct driver is SCR-E, not MEP-PH-1.

10. **MINOR — The RTU-1 E row states lu=12 ft, but the reported 42.4 psf is the value for lu floored to 20 ft.**
    - Requirement: criteria 5.4.1, "A fetch shorter than 20 ft is taken as lu = 20 ft".
    - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §2 table: "RTU-1 E 42.4, 36.0–43.6, lu=12.0 ft, leeward".
    - Recompute: hd(12)=1.376 ft, peak=30.5 psf; hd(20)=1.910 ft, peak=42.4 psf. The value uses the 20 ft floor;
      the stated lu=12 ft is inconsistent. Correct the basis to lu=20 ft (or, better, report the windward case as
      finding 2).

11. **MINOR — A few constraint-register rows carry numbers that are not in the cited clause/document, so they may
    count against the register under the task's rule.**
    - Row 58: cites EOR cl. 9.3 and 9.1 and gives "storey height of 32 ft"; 32 ft is stated in cl. 6.1, not 9.3/9.1.
    - Row 59: cites EOR cl. 9.1 and gives "6 ft span"; 6 ft is stated on S-101, not in cl. 9.1.

# Independent review — DC-2 Helena roof deck submission

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverable reviewed in place at
`/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task7_roof_deck_design__blind/output/submission.zip`
(zip root: `deck_design.xlsx`, `roof_deck_plan.dxf`, `constraint_register.xlsx`, `design_basis.md`).
The submission was not modified. Values below are independently recomputed from the project documents,
the IFC model and the catalogue, not copied from the author's tables.

Severity key: BLOCKING = a hard requirement or format rule is violated / a required item is not demonstrated;
MAJOR = a wrong value or conclusion, or a hard family left at material risk; MINOR = documentation/consistency.

---

1. **BLOCKING — The required 1.5 in deck bearing is not demonstrated and the author expressly concedes a 1.25 in
   bearing at panel-end joints.**
   - Requirement: EOR-DC-RD-01 Rev 2 cl. 10.6, "Deck is to bear not less than 1.5 in on each support";
     S-501 Rev 2 Detail 1, note B, "MINIMUM END BEARING IS 1-1/2 IN AT EVERY SUPPORT"; Joist and Joist Girder Schedule
     note N2, "The top chord bearing width ... 2.5 in ... is shared between the two deck sheets that lap on that
     interior joist."
   - Deliverable: `design_basis.md` §8 item 4 states: "At a panel-end (butt) joint each end therefore has 1.25 in,
     less than the 1.5 in minimum bearing of criteria 10.6 and note N1. The deck layout is set out to land panel ends
     on joists in a regular pattern; the erector is to confirm with the EOR that the joist top chord at those joints
     provides 1.5 in per panel end before that run is laid."
   - Should be: a deck layout/detail that provides 1.5 in bearing at every support (for example a lapped/nested
     support detail, an offset or filler panel, or a wider support), with the 2.5 in top chord explicitly accounted
     for. The current package leaves a hard bearing requirement open as an RFI.
   - Evidence: `design_basis.md` §6 simultaneously claims "1.5 in on the 2.5 in joist top chord"; that contradicts
     §8 item 4. The 2.5 in chord cannot give two full 1.5 in end bearings to two butted panel ends (3.0 in required).

# DC-2 Helena data centre — roof deck design for gravity and lateral loads

You are the structural engineer for Building A of the DC-2 data centre in Lewis and Clark County, Montana.
The roof framing is fixed and is not yours to change: open-web steel joists at 6 ft-0 in on centre spanning
30 ft between joist girders, over a 240 ft by 180 ft footprint, with the deck spanning across the joists in
three-span continuous conditions. Your job is the **roof deck**: its gage, its support-fastener pattern, its
sidelap connectors, and where each of those changes across the roof.

The project documents are in `project/`; the published standards the project cites are in `library/`; blank
deliverable templates are in `templates/`. The roof carries a rooftop equipment enclosure, equipment
screens, rooftop units, parapets and framed openings — the three-dimensional record of all of it is the
structural model in `project/15_model/`, and the two-dimensional drawings do not all agree with it or with
each other. Work out which documents govern and what they require.

The deck must carry the gravity loads, including the snow drifts the roof's own obstructions create; it must
carry the in-plane diaphragm shears from wind and seismic to the braced frames; its attachment must hold the
roof down under wind uplift; and among designs that do all of that, the lowest **installed cost** at the cost
plan rates is preferred.

The deck's shear stiffness is a result of your design, and the distribution of the roof force between the
eight braced frames depends on it — a stiffer deck does not simply have more capacity in reserve.

## Deliverable

Write one file, `output/submission.zip`, containing at its root:

### 1. `deck_design.xlsx` — the design (sheet names and column headers exactly as below)

All plan coordinates are **project grid coordinates in feet**: x along grids 1→9, y along grids A→G, origin
at grid 1-A.

* **Zones**: `zone_id`, `x0_ft`, `y0_ft`, `x1_ft`, `y1_ft`, `gage`, `support_pattern`, `sidelap_type`,
  `sidelap_per_span`. One row per **rectangle**. A zone may be made of several rectangles — repeat the
  `zone_id`, and every rectangle of a zone must carry the same gage, pattern, sidelap type and count. The
  rectangles must not overlap and together must cover every part of the roof that receives deck.
  `support_pattern` is written `36/n` for n fasteners across the 36 in cover width at each support.
* **DesignBasis**: `key`, `value` — one row per key, all of:
  `PG_PSF`, `CE`, `CT`, `IS`, `PF_PSF`, `GAMMA_PCF`, `LR_PSF`, `QH_PSF`, `A_ZONE_FT`, `SDS`, `IE`, `R`,
  `W_SEISMIC_PSF`, `FPX_KIP`, `WIND_X_KIP`, `WIND_Y_KIP`, `DIAPHRAGM_CLASS`.
  `W_SEISMIC_PSF` is the effective seismic weight per square foot of roof, `FPX_KIP` the roof diaphragm
  design force, `WIND_X_KIP` and `WIND_Y_KIP` the roof-level wind forces, `DIAPHRAGM_CLASS` the
  classification the design criteria ask for.
* **Drifts**: `location`, `face`, `peak_surcharge_psf`, `band_from_ft`, `band_to_ft` — one row for each
  of `MEP-PH-1` face `W`, `SCR-N` face `S`, `PARAPET` face `N`, `RTU-1` face `E`. `peak_surcharge_psf` is
  the drift surcharge at the face, over and above the balanced snow load; `band_from_ft` and `band_to_ft`
  are the plan coordinates bounding the drift, on the axis normal to that face — x for an east or west
  face, y for a north or south face — running from the face outwards. For `PARAPET` face `N`, the face is
  the inside of the north parapet.
* **CalcSummary**: `zone_id`, `governing_scenario`, `shear_demand_plf`, `shear_capacity_plf`,
  `gravity_demand_psf`, `gravity_capacity_psf`, `uplift_demand_psf`, `uplift_capacity_psf` — one row per
  zone, each demand being the largest anywhere in that zone over all scenarios, and `governing_scenario`
  the scenario id (`S01`…`S10`) whose demand/capacity ratio is the largest for that zone.
* **Diaphragm**: `scenario`, `direction`, `max_shear_plf`, `max_deflection_in`, `chord_force_kip`,
  `collector_force_kip`, `classification` — one row per lateral scenario.
* **BOM**: `item`, `quantity`, `unit` — at least `deck area <g> gage` in sf for every gage used,
  `support fasteners` and `sidelap connectors` in ea.

### 2. `roof_deck_plan.dxf` — the roof framing plan

In **feet**, in the same grid coordinates. One closed `LWPOLYLINE` per zone rectangle on layer
`S-DECK-ZONE`, and for each zone a `TEXT` label containing its `zone_id`, placed inside one of that zone's
rectangles, on layer `S-DECK-TEXT`. Show the framing on layer `S-FRAMING` and the roof openings on layer
`S-OPENING`.

### 3. `constraint_register.xlsx` — the requirements you designed to

Sheet `Register` with columns `document`, `clause`, `value`, `applies_to`: one row per requirement you
applied, naming the governing document (its title or document number), the clause, section or table, the
numerical value with units where there is one, and what it binds. Only the first 150 rows are read. A row
that cites a superseded or non-governing document, or whose value contradicts the clause it cites (it gives
a different number for a quantity that clause states), counts against the register; every number in a row
must be a value the cited clause states (or an equivalent of it), so one wrong number makes the row count
against the register even when another is right; rows without numbers do not count against it; a row that
cites requirements of more than one document or more than three clauses, or carries more than 8 numbers, is
not credited and counts against the register. If more than 40 % of the rows read count against the register,
none of it is credited. A requirement you satisfy but do not register earns less credit than one you satisfy
and register; a governing requirement missing from the register forfeits the credit of every family it governs.

### 4. `design_basis.md`

A narrative: which documents governed where they conflict and why, the snow and seismic bases, how the
diaphragm was analysed and classified, the zoning decisions and what drove each one.

## How the deliverable is judged

The design is re-analysed independently in every design scenario, with the loads, capacities and stiffnesses
derived from the project documents. Each scenario is credited for the constraints the design satisfies and
documents — hard constraints (gravity strength, deflection and bearing, diaphragm shear, in-plane
deflection, chord and collector forces, uplift, attachment rules, zoning rules, procurement, and the design
basis values) and softer documentation and consistency checks (schedule completeness, the drawing, the bill
of materials, the governing-scenario declaration). Cost credit is measured against a certified lower bound
on the installed cost of any compliant design: each scenario scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p is the
fraction of the 28 constraint families credited, h the fraction of the 21 hard families credited ([h = 1] is
1 when all 21 are, else 0), and O the bound divided by your installed cost, at most 1. A hard miss withholds
the cost credit.

            if ax>0 and ay>0: a-=ax*ay
        n=int(r['support_pattern'].split('/')[1]); ns=r['sidelap_per_span']
        area[g]=area.get(g,0)+a
        fast+=a/18.0*n
        side[(r['sidelap_type'])]=side.get(r['sidelap_type'],0)+a/18.0*ns
    rows=[dict(item='deck area %d gage'%g,quantity=round(area[g],1),unit='sf') for g in sorted(area)]

1 Codes and standards
1.1 The building code adopted by the authority having jurisdiction is the International Building Code as adopted and
amended by the State of Montana and by Lewis and Clark County, together with the referenced standard for
minimum design loads and associated criteria for buildings and other structures. All section numbers quoted in this
document without another source are sections of that adopted code.
1.2 The Department of Defense criteria overlay for this project is UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering. Where
UFC 3-301-01 replaces, supplements or adds to a provision of the adopted building code, the UFC provision
governs. Clauses of this document that rest on a UFC modification cite the UFC paragraph.
1.3 Minimum roof live loads are taken from UFC 3-301-01 Table E-1, not from the live load table of the adopted
code. Where Table E-1 and the adopted code differ, Table E-1 governs.
1.4 Cold-formed steel deck is designed to the North American specification for cold-formed steel structural
members; steel deck diaphragms are designed to the North American standard for the design of profiled steel
diaphragm panels. Open-web steel joists and joist girders are designed and supplied to the Steel Joist Institute
specifications. Hot-rolled steel members are designed to the AISC specification for structural steel buildings.
1.5 Thermal effects are excluded from the design of the roof deck and its attachments by agreement with the
authority having jurisdiction, recorded in the Owner's basis of design. Self-straining forces are not combined with
the load effects of section 8 of this document.

3.1 Rooftop equipment is supported on curbs carried by reinforced framing and is not treated as a uniform dead
load on the deck. Operating weights are given on the rooftop equipment schedule.
3.2 The roof dead weight used for the seismic effective weight is given in clause 7.2 and is broken down in the

4 Roof live load
4.1 Roof live load Lr is taken from UFC 3-301-01 Table E-1. For an ordinary flat roof that is not occupiable and is
not a roof garden or an assembly area, Table E-1 item 51 gives an unreduced roof live load of Lo = 20 psf.
4.2 Roof live load on the deck. The tributary-area reduction Lr = Lo R1 R2 applies only where the tributary area
exceeds 200 sq ft: for a tributary area At not exceeding 200 sq ft, R1 = 1.0. A deck panel's tributary area is the
panel cover width times the joist spacing, 3 ft x 6 ft = 18 sq ft, which is far below the 200 sq ft threshold, so no
reduction is available to the deck. The roof deck and its attachments are therefore designed for the
unreduced roof live load Lr = 20 psf. The slope reduction R2 is 1.0 for the roof slope used on this project.
4.3 The joists, joist girders and columns take the tributary-area reduction on their own tributary areas, subject to the
floor value of Lr = 12 psf. The reduced value is a member-by-member result and is not to be carried back into the
deck design; a deck designed for the reduced roof live load is not compliant with this document.
4.4 Roof live load is not combined with snow load; the larger of the two governs in the combinations of section 8.
Construction loading is covered by clause 9.1.
5 Snow loads
5.1 Flat roof snow load. pf = 0.7 Ce Ct Is pg, with the ground snow load pg = 63 psf from the site-specific case
study SNOW-2026-014, the exposure factor Ce = 0.90 (Terrain Category C, partially exposed roof - the roof carries
a continuous parapet, an equipment enclosure and rooftop units), and the thermal factor Ct = 1.0 (heated structure,
continuously conditioned). With Is = 1.10 from clause 2.1:
pf = 0.7 x 0.90 x 1.00 x 1.10 x 63 = 43.66 psf
Because pg exceeds 20 psf, the minimum roof snow load provision does not control and the rain-on-snow
surcharge is not required.
5.2 Snow density. gamma = 0.13 pg + 14, not greater than 30 pcf. For this site gamma = 0.13 x 63 + 14 = 22.19
pcf.
5.3 Balanced snow depth. hb = pf / gamma = 43.66 / 22.19 = 1.968 ft. All clear heights used for drift surcharges
are measured from the top of the balanced snow, that is, hc = h - hb where h is the height of the obstruction above
the roof surface.
5.4 Drift surcharges
The deck is governed by local drift surcharge over much of the roof, so the method is stated here in full and is to be
applied exactly as written.
5.4.1 Drift height. For an upwind fetch lu in feet,

hd = 0.43 lu^(1/3) (pg + 10)^(1/4) - 1.5 (ft)
with hd taken as zero if the expression is negative. A fetch shorter than 20 ft is taken as lu = 20 ft; there is no upper
limit on lu other than the roof itself.
5.4.2 Surcharge shape. A drift forming against an obstruction of clear height hc = h - hb is triangular, with its peak
at the face of the obstruction and falling linearly to zero at the far edge of the drift. Where hd is not greater than hc
the drift is full height: the peak surcharge is hd x gamma and the drift width is w = 4 hd. Where hd exceeds hc the
drift is truncated by the obstruction: the peak surcharge is hc x gamma and the width is w = min(4 hd^2 / hc, 8 hc).
The surcharge is added to the balanced load pf, and the balanced load acts over the whole roof including beneath
the drift.
5.4.3 Windward face. On the face that the wind arrives at, a windward drift of height 0.75 hd is taken, with lu
equal to the roof fetch from the upwind roof edge to that face.
5.4.4 Sheltered face. On the sheltered face, a leeward drift of height hd is taken, with lu equal to the along-wind
length of the obstruction itself, that is, the dimension of the obstruction measured in the direction the wind is
blowing. The roof of the obstruction is the snow source for that drift.
5.4.5 Wind directions. Wind is considered from each of the four directions in turn. Every obstruction forms a
windward drift on the face the wind arrives at and a leeward drift on its sheltered face in each direction. The design
surcharge at a point on the roof is the largest of the surcharges produced at that point by the four directions; the
four directions are not superimposed.
5.4.6 Parapets. A parapet is treated by the windward rule of clause 5.4.3: the drift height is 0.75 hd with lu equal to
the roof dimension upwind of the parapet, and the clear height is hc = parapet height above the roof surface minus
hb. The parapet on this project is 3 ft-6 in high on all four sides.
5.4.7 Application to the deck. The deck is a local element. Each deck zone must carry the peak surcharge
occurring anywhere within the area it serves, not the average over that area and not the value at its centre.
Where a drift crosses a zone boundary the higher demand governs the whole of the zone it falls in.
5.5 Snow buildup at rooftop obstructions
Per UFC 3-301-01 paragraph 3-4.1, which adopts ASCE 7-22 Section 7.4 [Supplement], snow buildup around
rooftop obstructions is to be considered. Rooftop equipment, equipment curbs, equipment enclosures and screen
walls are obstructions. An obstruction standing more than 2.0 ft above the balanced snow surface (that is, hc
greater than 2.0 ft) is treated as a drift obstruction and is given the full treatment of clause 5.4 on every face.
Shorter obstructions need not be given a drift surcharge, but the balanced load is carried across them.
5.5.1 The equipment enclosure, the equipment screen wall and the packaged rooftop units shown on the current
revision of the rooftop equipment plan and in the roof structure model are all obstructions within the meaning of this
clause. Their plan position and height are to be taken from the current revision of those documents.

recurrence interval is V = 115 mph (3-second gust). The surface roughness at the site is open country and the

9.1 Deck deflection. The deflection of the deck under the live or snow load, computed on the 3-span continuous
condition, must not exceed span / 240. Per UFC 3-301-01 section 1604.3.1 [Replacement], deflections must not
exceed the most restrictive of the deflection limits of the adopted building code or of UFC Table 2-1; the limit stated
here is that most restrictive value for this element. Construction-stage deflection of the bare deck under the erection
load is additionally limited to 0.75 in.
9.2 Diaphragm deflection. The in-plane deflection of the roof diaphragm under the design lateral load must not
exceed 1.60 in. The computed deflection includes the shear flexibility of the deck, the flexibility of the chords and
the flexibility of the connections, and is reported for each lateral case.
9.3 Diaphragm classification. The roof diaphragm is classified flexible when its computed maximum in-plane
deflection under the design lateral load exceeds 2.0 times the average storey drift of the vertical elements of
the seismic force-resisting system at that level; otherwise it is analysed as semi-rigid, with the diaphragm modelled
as an in-plane element of finite stiffness and the braced frames as springs of the stiffness published in the lateral
analysis report. The classification arrived at is to be computed, not assumed, and is to be stated in the design basis
submitted with the deck design. The allowable storey drift for Risk Category III is 0.015 times the storey height.

Schema: IFC4 (ISO-10303-21 physical file, ReferenceView_V1.2)

1.  UNITS
    The model is authored in MILLIMETRES.  IfcUnitAssignment declares LENGTHUNIT = MILLI METRE,
    AREAUNIT = MILLI SQUARE_METRE, VOLUMEUNIT = MILLI CUBIC_METRE and MASSUNIT = KILO GRAM.
    Every project drawing, schedule and calculation is inch-pound, so lengths read out of this
    model must be divided by 304.8 to obtain feet (1 ft = 304.8 mm, 1 in = 25.4 mm).
    Rooftop unit operating weights are published in this model in KILOGRAMS; they were converted
    from the pounds given in the mechanical equipment schedule at 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg.

2.  COORDINATE ORIGIN AND AXIS CONVENTION
    The model origin is the intersection of grid 1 and grid A, at finished floor.
      model +X  = project grid x, east, grids 1 -> 9 at 30 ft centres
      model +Y  = project grid y, north, grids A -> G at 30 ft centres
      model +Z  = up, measured from finished floor; z = 0 is finished floor
    The building footprint is 240 ft (x) by 180 ft (y).  The single IfcBuildingStorey is named
    ROOF and is placed at Elevation = 9753.6 mm, i.e. 32 ft above finished floor (top of
    steel at the main roof).  Every roof element is placed relative to that storey, so a local z of
    0.0 in an element placement is the roof datum and positive local z is above the roof surface.
    IfcSite and IfcBuilding placements are the identity; there is no rotation to true north other
    than the TrueNorth direction carried by the geometric representation context.

3.  WHAT IS MODELLED
    - IfcGrid "DC2-A ROOF GRID": U axes 1 through 9, V axes A through G, with their labels.
    - IfcColumn at every grid intersection, finished floor to roof (63 columns).
    - IfcBeam for every 26K9 joist: one beam per joist line per 30 ft bay, joist lines at
      6 ft centres in x, spanning in y between the joist girders (246 beams).
    - IfcBeam for every 36G 5N 15.0K joist girder: one beam per 30 ft bay along grids A through G
      (56 beams).
    - IfcMember for the braced-frame diagonals, two per braced bay, tagged BF-X1 ... BF-Y4
      (16 members).  Each braced frame carries Pset_BracedFrame with its wall line, bay and
      published roof-level stiffness.
    - IfcWall (PredefinedType PARAPET) for the four parapet runs, 3.5 ft above the roof.
    - IfcSlab (PredefinedType ROOF) for the roof deck area, voided by one IfcOpeningElement per
      framed roof opening (RO-1, RO-2, RO-3).
    - IfcBuildingElementProxy for every rooftop obstruction: the equipment enclosure MEP-PH-1, the
      equipment screen walls SCR-N and SCR-E, and rooftop units RTU-1, RTU-2, RTU-3, RTU-4, RTU-5, RTU-6, RTU-7, RTU-8, RTU-9, RTU-10, RTU-11, RTU-12.  Each carries its tag in
      Name and an IfcPropertySet "Pset_RoofObstruction" with HeightAboveRoof (mm); the rooftop units

    All bodies are real IfcExtrudedAreaSolid geometry over IfcRectangleProfileDef or
    IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef, placed with IfcLocalPlacement, so plan extents and heights can be
    read out of the geometry and not only out of the property sets.

4.  WHAT IS NOT MODELLED
    - The roof deck is shown as ONE slab of nominal 1.5 in thickness representing the
      1-1/2 in wide rib (Type B) deck profile.  Deck gage, deck zoning, support fastener patterns,

    - Section sizes used only as modelling envelopes: columns 12 in square, braced-frame

5.  STATUS

Owner's Basis of Design - Excerpt
Document OBD-DC2-A, Revision A. Extract of Sections 1, 3, 5 and 9 issued to the design and construction team for the roof structure package.
1  Project identification
Owner | Continental Divide Digital Infrastructure LLC
Project number | DC2-2026-014
Project name | DC-2 Helena Data Centre - Building A
Site | Lewis and Clark County, Montana (Canyon Ferry Road site, elevation 4,880 ft)
Site coordinates | 46.6832 N, 111.9756 W (WGS 84)
Facility type | Single-storey data centre, one enclosed data hall with a rooftop mechanical equipment yard
Risk category | Risk Category III
Structural engineer of record | Sandalwood Marlow Structural Engineers, PLLC
Date of this excerpt | 31 July 2026


3  Facility description
The building is a single-storey, single-occupancy data centre of 240 ft by 180 ft on plan, framed in structural steel, with the top of roof steel at elevation 32 ft-0 in above finished floor and a continuous 3 ft-6 in parapet on all four sides. The facility supports a designated emergency operations tenant and is therefore classified Risk Category III; the Owner requires that the classification be carried through every load case, including the roof snow and lateral cases, and that it not be traded away in value engineering.
A louvred equipment enclosure and a row of packaged rooftop units stand on the main roof within a screened yard. The roof structure runs continuously beneath the enclosure; the enclosure is not a separate roof level.
3.4  Roof framing and roof deck
The roof framing is open-web steel joists at 6 ft-0 in on centre spanning 30 ft-0 in between joist girders on the transverse column lines. The joist girders are supported on the perimeter columns and on the interior column lines.
The roof deck is to be 1.5 in wide-rib (Type B) steel deck of 3 ft-0 in cover width, spanning across the joists in continuous lengths of not less than three spans wherever the framing allows. The deck serves three functions at once - it carries the roof gravity load to the joists, it acts as the roof diaphragm delivering wind and seismic force to the braced frames, and it is the substrate for the roofing assembly - and the Owner expects a single deck package to satisfy all three.
Deck gage, support attachment and sidelap connection are to be developed by the structural engineer of record and are to be shown on the roof deck drawing as zones, so that the erector can set out the work without reference to a calculation package.
5  Programme and procurement
The roof structure package is on the critical path. The Owner's procurement strategy assumes that roof-deck material is on site and available to the erector within 9 weeks of release for fabrication. A deck product, gage or finish that cannot meet that allowance is not available to this project, whatever its structural merit, and the design is to be developed accordingly.
Release for fabrication of the roof deck package: on approval of the roof deck drawing and the deck attachment schedule.
Material on site: not later than 9 weeks after that release.
Substitutions that lengthen the delivery are to be raised with the Owner before they are carried into the design, not after.
9  Design exclusions and agreements with the authority having jurisdiction
The following have been agreed with the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) in the pre-application review and are recorded here so that they are not re-opened:
Thermal effects are excluded from the roof deck design. The roof assembly is fully insulated above the deck and the building is conditioned continuously; the AHJ has agreed that self-straining thermal forces need not be combined with the gravity, snow, wind or seismic effects in the design of the roof deck and its attachments.
The ground snow load for the site is established by a site-specific case study rather than by the mapped value. The study is a separate document and is the only source of the ground snow load for this project.
Roof drainage is by internal drains with secondary overflow scuppers through the parapet; ponding instability is addressed by the drainage design and by the deck stiffness requirements of the structural design criteria.
Nothing in this excerpt relieves the structural engineer of record of the obligation to apply the importance factors and load combinations required for Risk Category III.
